title: Phase 4 Exact-Method Implementation Account
description: The analyst's implementation account, available before independent theorist review. Retained source files use the scientific record's existing artifact pointers and digest checks. An unavailable execution or verification check must be stated explicitly; nonempty prose does not establish correctness.

rule.description: The procedure implemented from the exact selected method.

correspondence.description: Relevant algorithm steps or equations and exact retained code/configuration pointers, naming the execution properties actually checked and any unavailable correspondence. Preserve the distinction between a checked implementation property and an exact execution guarantee.

environment.description: The actual shared runtime, dependencies and settings, including any access limitation.

verification.description: Checks actually performed, their scope and retained support; state unavailable or unassessed checks and their limits. Finite tests or higher precision do not establish a universal exact execution guarantee.

limitations.description: Unresolved departures, verification gaps and their consequences.

invocation.description: Ordinary command and input/output contract using the final declared filenames, including seed behavior. Distinguish example execution from retained-table regeneration and simulation reruns, naming required inputs and unavailable tasks honestly. Do not claim an unexecuted command was checked. No harness paths, provider account or required MODEL_FORGE_* variables.

runtime_identity.description: Actual shared interpreter identity/version, or the precise access/setup limitation.

reproduction.description: Portable model code and synthetic example reconciled against the final declared source files. Check README filenames, commands, inputs and dependencies against that inventory. Distinguish the standalone example, regeneration of retained tables from saved rows and rerunning simulations, with the files and inputs each needs or an explicit limitation. An unavailable bundle uses null for missing files and explains the limitation in the existing account; neither prose nor a declared command proves successful execution.
